markdown.headingText: Course Portal: IB Mathematics AI HL (Applications & Interpretation)
markdown.markdown:
::: {.callout-note} Welcome, students! This specialized section contains syllabus breakdowns, core study notes, targeted practice question banks, and actual exam past papers organized dynamically to optimize your learning and help you achieve a Grade 7. ::: ## 1. Course Introduction

Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (AI) Higher Level (HL) focuses on the practical applications of mathematics in real-world contexts, modeling economic and physical systems, and advanced statistics and probability. It emphasizes the extensive use of technology and graphing software to solve complex, data-driven problems. It is highly recommended for students planning to pursue Economics, Finance, Data Science, Business, or Applied Sciences at top universities.

### Assessment Outline

The IB Mathematics AI HL course is assessed through three final written examinations (80%) and an independent mathematical exploration task (20%). A graphic display calculator (GDC) is required for all written examinations:

Assessment Component Duration Calculator Policy Marks Weighting
Paper 1 (Short Questions) 120 minutes (2 hours) Calculator required (GDC required) 110 marks 30%
Paper 2 (Long Questions) 120 minutes (2 hours) Calculator required (GDC required) 110 marks 30%
Paper 3 (Problem Solving) 60 minutes (1 hour) Calculator required (GDC required) 55 marks 20%
Internal Assessment (IA) - Exploration Independent research (12-20 pages) No restrictions 20 marks 20%
### Syllabus Structure

The syllabus is organized into five core topics consisting of both standard core content and advanced high-level extension topics (SL Core & HL Extensions):

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Topic 1: Number and algebra **1.1**: Operations in standard form
**1.2**: Arithmetic sequences and series
**1.3**: Geometric sequences and series
**1.4**: Financial applications
**1.5**: Laws of exponents with integer exponents
**1.6**: Approximation and significant figures
**1.7**: Amortization and annuities using technology
**1.8**: Systems of linear equations and polynomial solutions
**1.9**: Laws of logarithms [AHL]
**1.10**: Expressions with rational exponents [AHL]
**1.11**: Complex numbers in Cartesian form [AHL]
**1.12**: Polar and exponential forms of complex numbers [AHL]
**1.13**: Matrix operations and determinant [AHL]
**1.14**: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalization [AHL] ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Topic 2: Functions **2.1**: Straight lines: equations, gradient, intercepts
**2.2**: Concept of a function: domain, range, notation
**2.3**: Graphs of functions
**2.4**: Key features of graphs
**2.5**: Financial and modeling applications
**2.6**: Mathematical modeling process
**2.7**: Composite and inverse functions [AHL]
**2.8**: Advanced graph transformations [AHL]
**2.9**: Modeling and fitting data [AHL] ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Topic 3: Geometry and trigonometry **3.1**: Distance and midpoint in 3D space
**3.2**: Right-angled trigonometry
**3.3**: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle
**3.4**: Circle geometry: arc length and sector area
**3.5**: Equations of perpendicular bisectors
**3.6**: Voronoi diagrams
**3.7**: Logistic models [AHL]
**3.8**: Trigonometric definitions in unit circle [AHL]
**3.9**: Geometric transformations with matrices [AHL]
**3.10**: Concept of vectors [AHL]
**3.11**: Vector equations of lines [AHL]
**3.12**: Vector kinematics [AHL]
**3.13**: Scalar product and angle between vectors [AHL]
**3.14**: Graph theory: vertices, edges, degree [AHL]
**3.15**: Adjacency matrices and walks [AHL]
**3.16**: Algorithms for trees and cycles, MST, TSP [AHL] ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Topic 4: Statistics and probability **4.1**: Population, sampling, discrete and continuous data
**4.2**: Data presentation: frequency distributions
**4.3**: Measures of central tendency and dispersion
**4.4**: Bivariate data, correlation, and regression
**4.5**: Probability of events, Venn and tree diagrams
**4.6**: Independent and mutually exclusive events
**4.7**: Discrete random variables and expectation
**4.8**: Binomial distribution
**4.9**: Normal distribution
**4.10**: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient
**4.11**: Chi-squared tests for independence and goodness of fit
**4.12**: Data collection design and sampling [AHL]
**4.13**: Non-linear regression models [AHL]
**4.14**: Linear transformations of random variables [AHL]
**4.15**: Combinations of normal variables [AHL]
**4.16**: Confidence intervals [AHL]
**4.17**: Poisson distribution [AHL]
**4.18**: Hypothesis testing and critical regions [AHL] ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Topic 5: Calculus **5.1**: Introduction to limits
**5.2**: Increasing and decreasing functions
**5.3**: Derivative of power functions and basic rules
**5.4**: Tangents and normals equations
**5.5**: Indefinite integration as anti-differentiation
**5.6**: Stationary points and local maximum/minimum
**5.7**: Optimization problems
**5.8**: Trapezoidal rule for approximating areas
**5.9**: Derivatives of standard functions [AHL]
**5.10**: Second derivative and concavity [AHL]
**5.11**: Indefinite and definite integration [AHL]
**5.12**: Volumes of revolution [AHL]
**5.13**: Differential equations and modeling [AHL]
**5.14**: Slope fields [AHL]
**5.15**: Euler's method [AHL]
**5.16**: Coupled systems of differential equations [AHL] ::: ::: {.download-box} ### Official Academic Resources *Download official IB resources and curriculum guides below (Google Drive links will be loaded from metadata):*
